info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

post.description:
F6-T7: shares `quantity` units of a product at a location over the lines
waiting for them, highest priority and oldest order first.

409.description: Another allocation for this product and location is running

post.description:
F6-T6: marks the hold released, with who and why; the order can then be
released once no other hold is open.

422.description: An empty or too long note

get.description:
F6-T17: every line of the order's fulfilment orders with ordered,
shipped, delivered and backordered quantities, the promised date, and the
shipments carrying it.

post.summary: Override where a fulfilment order ships from
post.description:
F6-T4: before the order is released (`draft` or `on_hold`), a person with
`fulfilment_order.override_sourcing` names the location instead of the
sourcing rules; who did it is kept on the order.

200.description: The fulfilment order ships from the new location

422.description: The order is already released, or the location is not an enabled stock location

post.description:
F6-T8: records the packages as one shipment (with a line per goods line
still to ship) and marks the order `packed`.

409.description: The order is not released or being picked

422.description: No packages, too many, or a size that is not positive

get.description: F6-T8: the goods still to ship, one group per product.

post.description:
F6-T6: opens the holds the order should carry, then refuses while any
hold is open; otherwise the order is `released` for picking.

409.description: A hold is open, or the order is not a draft or on hold

post.summary: Book a shipment with its carrier
post.description:
Books a packed shipment with its carrier and stores the waybill as its
tracking number (status `booked`). Weight and pieces default to the
shipment's packages.

409.description: Already booked or being booked, or the carrier is not set up

422.description: A missing consignee field, or the carrier refused the booking

post.description:
The shipment's driver starts the delivery; with delivery codes on, the
customer is texted a code.

403.description: Caller lacks delivery_proof.create or is not the shipment's driver

post.description:
The shipment's driver records delivered, a failed attempt or a refusal,
with photo, signature, the customer's code (when codes are on), who
received it and where. A delivery with cash on delivery records the
cash payment.

403.description: Caller lacks delivery_proof.create (or, for cash on delivery, customer_payment.create) or is not the shipment's driver

409.description: The shipment is already closed, or too many wrong codes

422.description: A bad outcome or position, or a wrong or missing code

post.description:
Reads the latest update of the shipment's waybill from its carrier and
moves the shipment's status when the update is new.

409.description: The shipment is not booked with a carrier

AllocateBody.description: Newly available stock to give to waiting lines.

Allocated.description: One line and what it got.

description.description: What is inside, for customs and the label.

pieces.description: Pieces; the number of packages when absent.

weight_kg.description: Total weight; the packages' weights when absent.

note.description: Why the hold no longer applies (1 to 500 characters).

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

code_sent.description: A delivery code was texted to the customer.

Overridden.description: The fulfilment order after an override.

OverrideBody.description: The location to ship from instead.

PackBody.description: The packages an order went into.

PickGroup.description: One group of a pick list: a product and how many to pick.

otp.description: The customer's delivery code, when codes are on.

photo.description: A photo, already uploaded through the files API (its file key).

signature.description: A signature image, already uploaded (its file key).

cod_payment_id.description: The cash payment recorded for cash on delivery.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

label_url.description: The carrier's label, when it returned one.

Tracked.description: A shipment's status after a tracking read.

changed.description: Whether this read moved the shipment.

last_event_key.description: The carrier's latest update code, when it has one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
